rule: Keep only the solid 5x5 squares and crop to their bounding box plus a one-cell background border. In each square of colour c, paint background into the inner 3x3 wherever the c-coloured 3x3 glyph has paint. The glyph is inverted and never rotated. Glyphs with no matching square are discarded.
scope: Use same-colour 3x3 glyphs as negative stamps in 5x5 squares; crop the square lattice with a one-cell margin.

authored_scope:
Supported in random scenes:
- Background colour from 0..9.
- A stride-6 square lattice of 1..4 by 1..4 squares, 2..9 in total, with distinct colours. Lattices beyond 1x3, 2x2 and 3x2 are synthetic extensions.
- 0..3 distractor glyph colours.
- Uniformly random glyph masks of 3..7 cells that fill their 3x3 bounding box; disconnected masks are allowed.
- A glyph block on any of the four sides, with spacing 1..2, optional empty slots, separation 1..3 and random margins.
- Grids up to 30x30.

Not supported:
- Irregular square spacing.
- Squares sharing a colour.
- Glyphs interleaved among the squares.
- Squares that are not 5x5, and glyph sizes other than 3x3.
authored_constraints: Each square colour is distinct and differs from the background; each glyph colour is unique.
Every square colour has exactly one glyph of the same colour, so the mapping is unambiguous.
Each glyph touches all four sides of its 3x3 box, so the bounding-box extraction recovers the glyph exactly.

Glyphs are separated from each other by at least one background cell, and from the square block by at least one full background row or column. This gives no incidental connectivity, including diagonal contact.
The squares keep a one-cell background margin inside the grid, so the crop never clips.
The background is strictly the most frequent colour; this is checked on the drawn grid.
Output size always differs from input size, so no sample is an identity.
